translations.text: The world, as we lived in defilement, drunkenness, excess, drinking, and filthy idol worship, living in malice and envy, being hateful and hating one another, being disobedient and going astray, living in the emptiness of our hearts, being darkened in our thoughts and estranged from the life of God because of the ignorance within us and the hardness of our hearts. We had given ourselves over to defilement and to practicing every kind of impurity. But now we were not taught this way. Rather, we were taught: “Work toward your salvation with fear and trembling, for God is the one working in you both to will and to carry out that will.”
But now we were not taught this way. Rather, we were taught: “Work toward your salvation with fear and trembling, for God is the one working in you both to will and to carry out that will.”

For in those days Moses saw how readily the children of Israel forgot God's commandments. He commanded them to make tassels on the edges of their clothes, so that they would see them and remember God's commandments and not forget them. We too, however, should place the fear of God in our hearts instead of tassels, so that we will not forget the commandments our fathers handed down to us.

Therefore, brothers, let us turn back and repent before the opportunity slips away from us, and while the light is with us—that is, the teachings of our fathers—as the Lord said: “Walk while you have the light, so that the darkness does not overtake you.” And: “Let us conduct ourselves decently, as in the daytime.” And: “For those who sleep sleep at night, and those who get drunk get drunk at night. But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith”

You share in the suffering of those who are bound, that is, those who are afflicted, as they live on the wild greens of the field because they have found nothing to eat, as you hear. And those who see them testify to their suffering.
Therefore, let us all pray, everyone who fears God, that Christ may keep his blessing enduring in his congregations and not let his places lack anything.

We submit to regulations in the world like those who are alive: “Do not touch, do not taste, do not go near.” That is to say, we came out of the sins of the world and left them behind us. Why are we turning back again and wallowing in them? This is also what he said: “For at that time you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light, for the fruit of light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth, as you discern what pleases the Lord. And do not share in the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them. For the things they do secretly are shameful even to speak about. But everything that is exposed is made visible by the light, for everything made visible is light.” Therefore, let us too rebuke our foolishness within us, and all the thoughts of the devil that he throws into us, and unbelief and hatred, since they make us think evil against one another, even though we are not near one another at all. And we find fault with one another, rather than with ourselves, as though our struggle were against one another and not against the rulers and authorities, against the world rulers of darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavens, and not against blood and flesh. As the apostle said: “Take up the full armor of God, so that you can stand against the devil's schemes, for our struggle is not against blood and flesh.”

Also in connection with this, he said, “For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light, for the fruit of light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth. Test what is pleasing to the Lord, and do not share in the fruitless works of darkness, but rather expose them.”
For the things they do in secret are shameful even to mention. But all things are revealed when they are exposed by the light, for everything that is revealed is light.

Therefore, let us too rebuke our foolishness within us, and all the thoughts of the devil that he casts into us, along with unbelief and hatred. These make us think evil of one another even when we are not together at all, finding fault with one another and not with ourselves, as though our struggle were against one another and not against the rulers and authorities, against the world rulers of darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavens, and not against flesh and blood. As the apostle said, “Take up the full armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the devil’s schemes, for our struggle is not against flesh and blood.”

And we find fault with one another and not with ourselves, as though our struggle were against one another and not against the rulers and authorities, against the world rulers of darkness, against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavens, and not against flesh and blood.
As the apostle said, “Take up the full armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the devil’s schemes, for our struggle is not against flesh and blood.”

Therefore, be watchful, and let us hold firmly to what is good. For many are together in body but far apart in heart and love. And many others are not together in body but are together at all times in the love of Christ, the love of the Spirit, and the will of Jesus.
But you, brothers, keep and persevere in the things we have been taught. Many will learn and benefit from you, as he said, “Let them see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.”

For just as you have followed all the saints in your actions—as he said, “But you have followed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my endurance, my persecutions, and my sufferings”—continue to follow them by guarding your own labors. For those who possess the imperishable wealth in Christ are themselves responsible for watching over it.

If those who possess money, gold, silver, and property keep watch so that robbers do not steal them, how much more should we keep watch so that the enemy does not steal the good that we do: our prayers, our fasts, our purity, and our endurance.

For the theft of silver and gold is not the only loss. Rather, just as virginity and the monastic life are honored, so the enemy is eager to steal them. Someone who has acquired pearls or gold stays up at night keeping watch. If the enemy stays up at night [?] for the sake of evil, how much more will the person who owns the valuables keep watch, so that no one plots against them.

Let us remember what our fathers said: There are brothers who follow our way of life, fasting and praying, and spending the night keeping watch, yet also lying, fighting, quarreling, grumbling, and slandering. They hate, walk with an alienated heart, defile themselves, and practice deceit, doing every kind of evil. People like these suffer hardship in vain, and no benefit will come to them. Their endurance is also in vain, according to what was said: “A sieve does not fill up to produce flour.” And again, in this saying: “Sow wheat, and you will reap thorns.” Their allotted portions will not benefit them.
According to what was said: “A sieve does not fill up to produce flour.” And again, in this saying: “Sow wheat, and you will reap thorns.” Their allotted portions will not benefit them.

Therefore, be watchful. Do not let the enemy destroy the good we do. Instead, with all vigilance, guard our heart against every defiled thought of the devil, so that we may be worthy to hear this with a united heart: “From that time onward they will no longer serve a stranger, but will serve the Lord their God.”

For robbers do not break into a house or a place with no valuables in it. Instead, they break into a place where they will find valuables. Nor do they break into a place where people are keeping watch, in order to steal. Rather, the places they break into are those where they know people are not keeping watch and are forgetful, and they seize whatever they find. In the same way, the devil does not rob someone who keeps watch and guards the fruits of his labor for himself. Rather, someone whom he finds not keeping watch, not fearing God, and not thinking about how he will fall into God's hands, but drifting with every wind—that is the person whose good deeds he plunders without mercy.

In the same way, the devil does not rob someone who keeps watch and guards the fruits of his labor for himself. Rather, someone whom he finds not keeping watch, not fearing God, and not thinking about how he will fall into God's hands, but drifting with every wind—that is the person whose good deeds he plunders without mercy.

Therefore, brothers and sisters, everyone who is of one heart with God and with our fathers, and also with us, whether male or female, great or small, among us or among you: be steadfast and watchful. Let us not give sleep to our eyes or slumber to our eyelids until the Lord rescues us from every temptation of the enemy. For many envy us. And do not let the sight of brothers and sisters repeatedly becoming agitated amid fighting and quarrelling, and abandoning their endurance, cause you to stumble. But God forbid that they should ever cause those who love God to stumble—those whose faith in Christ is complete and who hold fast to the Spirit of God.

And do not let the sight of brothers and sisters repeatedly becoming agitated amid fighting and quarrelling, and abandoning their endurance, cause you to stumble. But God forbid that they should ever cause those who love God to stumble—those whose faith in Christ is complete and who hold fast to the Spirit of God.

But you who sin and abandon your endurance and disturb the congregations through faintheartedness, envy, hatred, fighting, quarrelling, and deceit: woe to you! What will you do on the day when you are called to account? For your distress is coming from afar.

Or is it not grounds for judgment against us if, after renouncing what we renounced and making an agreement with the one with whom we made an agreement in a covenant, declaring, 'We will not steal; we will not lie; we will not defile our bodies in any way; we will not bear false witness; we will not practice any deceit in secret,' along with the other statements that follow these, we turn back again and do these things once more?

Have you given glory to God? Stand up. I am speaking to you, Aphthonia, daughter of Count Alexander. Or have you honored the place where you were brought up [?], in matters concerning God and the world, through your words and deeds? If your heart had not become corrupt, you would not have disgraced the place where you are, or dishonored the brothers and sisters who are there with you. They call you by your name, Aphthonia, yet you envy yourself and direct your malice against yourself, wanting to destroy your soul, of which the whole world is not worthy, and to waste your labors for nothing. For you have given Satan room within you to change your heart and lead people astray like wild sheep. You foolish, ignorant woman, who has no instruction! For if you had understanding, even if they really had fought with you, you ought to let people know what you are like inside your community.
If your heart had not become corrupt, you would not have disgraced the place where you are, or dishonored the brothers and sisters who are there with you.

You foolish, ignorant woman, who has no instruction! For if you had understanding, even if they really had fought with you, you ought to let people know what you are like inside your community.

Especially since you told your father and your mother, 'They fought with me,' or, 'They insulted me,' lying when they neither fought with you nor insulted you. Did they fight with you because they gave you instruction when you broke the commandment and took things from your fathers without asking?

What did you ask for that you needed, only for them to turn you away or not give it to you? If you tell your father and your mother, are we afraid—especially when you are lying? So do you want us to tell them about the foolish deeds you commit, your thefts, and your quarrels?

You truly blind woman, groping at noon like those in the middle of the night, and like blind people who have no eyes! How can your fathers out in the world hear what you say here inside, while we in the convent do not know it?

If they really wronged you, oppressed you, or caused you grief, you should have told us about your suffering, so that we could know whether you were telling the truth or not. Or you should have told your mother who is there with you—if you do not merely call her “Mother” with your mouth while your heart is far from her, as it is written: “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.”

For if your undisciplined heart had not darkened you, would you have despised your fathers who are in the congregation with you? Or would you have insulted the sisters with whom you live, in your arrogance and your contempt for others?

Or if you had not abandoned instruction and understanding, and loved evil more than good, would you have rehearsed disgusting words and said with your mouth, which is full of curses and bitterness, “I will go to other convents”?

How has this place wronged you? Or what burden have they laid on you, except that they told you, “Do not transgress God's commandment”? For you have become self-indulgent, and [?] a young girl who lives in the house with you, so that you become a stumbling block and a cause of sin to one another.

Therefore, I declare to you that if you fail to pay attention to yourself and rid yourself of this disobedience and these pointless quarrels, I will make their hearts grieve, and I will make them deal with you according to what came out of their mouths.

Truly, I am distressed about you—or about all of you—because I fear that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your hearts may be corrupted and led away from the sincerity and purity directed toward Christ. If he did not leave that woman alone in paradise, will he spare you, or all of you, when you give him room within yourselves and accept his deceitful schemes and his evil deeds? For he cannot overpower those who fear God, those for whom Christ is a helper and protector, as it is written: “The one who fights for you is your helper, and the sword of your boasting and the glory of the firmament.” Whoever loves evil will be destroyed, and it is that person whom the devil will overpower through his soul-killing deeds. But the wise person who loves instruction will accept the commandment, and the person of understanding who fears the Lord will obtain a guide.

Nevertheless, let me hear that you have put your fathers who are there with you at ease, and obey them in everything, so that our hearts may be at ease, and you yourself may enjoy your peace of mind.

And if you have something to say, look: the elders, our fathers and our brothers, have come to you. Tell it to them. And all of you, if you have something to say or any matter in your community, do not hesitate to tell them, and do not hide anything from them, so that all our hearts may be at ease together, both ours and yours, and so that the Lord may also be pleased with us.

Oh, how complacent you are, you who give Satan room to enter and defile God's holy places, and who defile his temple, which is you yourselves! Have you not remembered the apostle's declaration: “Whoever defiles God's temple, God will destroy that person”?

Nor did you remember all the curses that our father pronounced when he entrusted us all to God, saying, “Cursed is anyone who defiles his body in any way, or steals any object, from a piece of cloth or a belt—especially clothing, bedding, or a head covering—down to the smallest item of food, whether from the supplies of God’s ministry or from the hands of those beside them.”
I had intended to come to you in unity of heart. But sorrow over those who angered God and grieved his Holy Spirit prevented our joy.

I know that I deserve every sorrow. But if God and our Lord Jesus are willing, I will come to you in anger and do to these undisciplined people and these foolish virgins, who have no oil in their vessels, everything that is in my heart. For once again you turn back to these ways of provoking God and fall under the sword of the evil one, who destroyed the whole inhabited world through his sins and his lawless deeds, because you loved defilement more than purity and chose death for yourselves rather than life.

For once again you turn back to these ways of provoking God and fall under the sword of the evil one, who destroyed the whole inhabited world through his sins and his lawless deeds, because you loved defilement more than purity and chose death for yourselves rather than life.

For you turned your backs on the one who created you and nourished you, God who lives forever. You also grieved the one who welcomed you, Jerusalem, that is, the congregation. And you fell at midday like those in the middle of the night, as it is written: “The virgin of Israel stumbled and fell; she will not rise again.”

For he said, “Those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.” But you have stumbled at midday like those of whom it was said, “Those who are drunk without wine.” And you have dozed at midday like those who sleep at night, because you abandoned the fear of God, loving darkness more than light. You also considered what is bitter to be sweet, and what is sweet to be bitter.
Therefore, woe to you wicked people, because you did not remember all the hardship our father endured with all of you. You abandoned his life-giving teachings and the [?] of your fathers.
Nevertheless, look, the elders are coming, and our brothers have come to you again, while we live in great grief and overwhelming sorrow, to deal with each one of you as she deserves.

Because you abandoned the spring of living water and dug cracked cisterns for yourselves, your undisciplined heart became dark. While saying, “We are wise,” you became foolish, exchanging the glory of God for improper deeds. Therefore God handed you over to shameful passions, namely theft, defilement, and every evil. Those who do these things face every punishment, not only in this age but also in the next.
